title: Sensor Hierarchy: construction order, protected interface, name hiding
hints: Each class logs in its own constructor BODY and destructor body. The language orders everything else: base, then members, then body, and the reverse on destruction.
Derived constructors must initialise the base explicitly: `Lidar(...) : Sensor(std::move(name), rate_hz), rings_(rings)`.
Lidar::describe() hides Sensor::describe(). Call the base version explicitly: `Sensor::describe() + " rings=" + std::to_string(rings_)`.
Throw from the Lidar constructor BEFORE logging "Lidar(...)". The already-built base and members are then destroyed automatically, but ~Lidar() never runs.
